10-k.txt:1716: Business
10-k.txt:1717: ABOUT US
10-k.txt:1718: Netflix, Inc. (“Netflix”, the “Company”, “registrant”, “we”, or “us”) is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.
10-k.txt:1719: Our core strategy is to grow our business globally within the parameters of our operating margin target. We strive to continuously improve our members' experience by offering compelling content that delights them and attracts new members. We aim to offer a range of pricing plans, including our ad-supported subscription plan, to meet a variety of consumer needs. We seek to drive conversation around our content to further enhance member joy, and we are continuously enhancing our user interface to help our members more easily choose content that they will find enjoyable.
10-k.txt:1720: BUSINESS SEGMENTS
10-k.txt:1721: We operate as one operating segment. Our revenues are primarily derived from monthly membership fees for services related to streaming content to our members. See Note 13,
10-k.txt:1722: Segment and Geographic Information
10-k.txt:1723: , in the accompanying notes to our consolidated financial statements for further detail.
10-k.txt:1724: COMPETITION
10-k.txt:1725: The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change. We compete with a broad set of activities for consumers’ leisure time, including other entertainment video providers, such as linear television, streaming entertainment providers (including those that provide pirated content), video gaming providers, open content platform providers, which provide access to user-generated and professionally produced content, as well as more broadly against other sources of entertainment, such as social media, that our members could choose in their moments of free time. We also compete against entertainment video providers and content producers in obtaining content for our service, both for licensed content and for original content projects.
10-k.txt:1726: While consumers may maintain simultaneous relationships with multiple entertainment sources, we strive for consumers to choose us in their moments of free time. We have often referred to this choice as our objective of “winning moments of truth.” In attempting to win these moments of truth with our members, we seek to continually improve our service, including both our technology and our content offerings.

10-k.txt:1729: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
10-k.txt:1730: We regard our trademarks, service marks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade dress, trade secrets, proprietary technologies and similar intellectual property as important to our success. We use a combination of patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret laws and confidentiality agreements to protect our proprietary intellectual property. Our intellectual property rights extend to our technology, business processes, the content we produce and distribute through our service, and the consumer products and experiences based thereon. We use the intellectual property of third parties in creating some of our content, merchandising our products and marketing our service. Our ability to provide our members with content they can watch depends on studios, content providers and other rights holders licensing rights, including distribution rights, to such content and certain related elements thereof, such as the public performance of music contained within the content we distribute. The license periods and the terms and conditions of such licenses vary. Our ability to protect and enforce our intellectual property rights is subject to certain risks and from time to time we encounter disputes over rights and obligations concerning intellectual property. We cannot provide assurance that we will prevail in any intellectual property disputes.
10-k.txt:1731: REGULATION
10-k.txt:1732: The media landscape and the internet delivery of content have seen growing regulatory action. Historically, media has been highly regulated in many countries. We are seeing some of these legacy regulatory frameworks be updated and expanded to address services like ours. In particular, we are seeing some countries update their cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix. This includes investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas. Some even restrict the extent of ownership rights we can have both in our service and in our content. In certain countries, regulators are also looking at restrictions that could require formal reviews of and/or adjustments to content that appears on our service in their country. In general these regulations impact all services and may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive as to the content offerings we may provide.
10-k.txt:1733: HUMAN CAPITAL
10-k.txt:1734: Our business is to entertain the world across different countries, cultures, languages and tastes. To entertain an audience this global, our Company needs to reflect the world and the variety of stories we tell. To help ensure our workforce is representative of the members we serve, we employ people in multiple countries around the world and work to maintain a global culture of inclusion. We view our employees and our culture as key to our success. As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 16,000 full-time employees. Of these, approximately 10,900 (68%) were located in the United States and Canada, 2,500 (16%) in Europe, Middle East, and Africa, 1,900 (12%) in Asia-Pacific and 700 (4%) in Latin America. We also have a number of employees engaged in content production, some of whom are part-time or temporary, and whose numbers fluctuate throughout the year and may be covered by collective bargaining agreements.
10-k.txt:1735: We believe an important component of our success is our company culture as detailed in the “Netflix Culture Memo”, which was updated in 2024. Our culture is focused on excellence and creating an environment where talented people can thrive — lifting ourselves, each other and our audiences higher and higher. We engage employees and seek feedback through regular town halls, surveys, business reviews and memos, which we often share broadly, inviting comments. We aim to attract and retain great people — representing a broad array of perspectives and skills — to work together as a dream team. For more people and cultures to see themselves reflected on screen, it is important that our employee base represents the communities we serve.
10-k.txt:1736: We aim generally to pay our employees at their personal top of market, and they generally are able to choose the form of their compensation between cash and stock options. This permits employee compensation to be highly personalized and reflective of each employee's individual needs and preferences. We conduct pay equity analyses at least annually, and have adopted practices to help ensure that employees from underrepresented groups are not being underpaid based on gender identity (globally) and race or ethnicity (United States (“U.S.”)) relative to others doing the same or similar work under comparable circumstances. We aim to rectify any pay gaps that we find through this analysis.
10-k.txt:1737: We care about the health and well-being of our employees and their families and provide a variety of benefit programs based on region, including health benefits. In the U.S., employees generally receive an annual cash health benefit allowance that they may allocate to medical, dental and vision premiums in a way that makes sense for them. Employees have access to a host of other benefits, including mental health, childcare, family planning and a company match for charitable donations.
10-k.txt:1738: We believe that our approach to human capital resources has been instrumental in our growth, and has made Netflix a desirable destination for employees.

We make available, free of charge on our website, access to our Annual Report on Form 10-K, our Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, our Current Reports on Form 8-K and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), as soon as reasonably practicable after we file or furnish them electronically with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”).

We use these channels as well as social media and blogs to communicate with our members and the public about our company, our services and other issues. It is possible that the information we post on social media and blogs could be deemed to be material information. exhibit-99-1.txt:60: Q3 Results and Forecast
exhibit-99-1.txt:61: Revenue in Q3 grew 12% year over year (+11% on a foreign exchange (F/X) neutral basis), and was in-line with our forecast. In Q3, revenue growth was driven primarily by subscription revenue, reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, growth in advertising revenue and a favorable impact from F/X rates, net of hedging. Membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast.
exhibit-99-1.txt:62: Q3’26 operating income totaled $4.5B (+37% year over year) and operating margin of 34.6% was up versus 28.2% in Q3’25. Both Q3 operating income and margin were ahead of forecast due primarily to the timing of expenses and the slight upside in revenue. As a result, diluted EPS for the quarter amounted to $0.87 vs. $0.59 in Q3’25 (+49% year over year).
exhibit-99-1.txt:63: As a reminder, the guidance we provide is our actual internal forecast at the time we report and we strive for accuracy. Our primary financial metrics are revenue for growth and operating margin for profitability. Our goal is to sustain healthy revenue growth, expand operating profit and margin, and deliver growing free cash flow.
exhibit-99-1.txt:64: In Q4, we expect revenue of $13.4 billion, which represents year over year growth of 12% (or 11% F/X neutral) driven by growth in memberships, pricing, and ad revenue. We project a Q4 operating margin of 26.0% which includes ~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions, and compares with 24.5% in the year ago quarter. These organizational changes enable us to continue to aggressively invest in high impact areas to improve our service, and drive growth and innovation.
exhibit-99-1.txt:65: Our guidance for Q4 means that for the full year 2026 we expect revenue of $51.1B, or growth of 13% (+12% on a F/X neutral basis). This is 0.2% below the mid-point of our prior 2026 revenue forecast range - while subscription revenue growth has outperformed our expectations, we currently expect 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7B vs. approximately $3B previously (due to slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities). We anticipate an operating margin of 31.5% for 2026 (31.4% based on F/X rates as of January 1, 2026) vs. 29.5% in 2025. Our updated 2026 margin guidance includes ~30 basis points negative impact associated with our Q4 headcount reductions. Our forecast implies annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:66: Our Focus
exhibit-99-1.txt:67: Our mission is to entertain the world while building a wildly successful business. # Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving its primary revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a secondary, non-material revenue stream from advertisements, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721, 10-k.txt:2073). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% year-over-year increase, and operating income of $13,326,603 thousand, resulting in an operating margin of 29.5% (10-k.txt:2058, 10-k.txt:2060, 10-k.txt:2061). Management has shifted its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin, discontinuing the reporting of average paying memberships and average monthly revenue per paying membership (10-k.txt:2063). The company maintains a competitive position by competing for consumers' "moments of truth" against a broad set of leisure activities, including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1726).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 5/5**
Netflix demonstrates strong business-model durability through its transition to a highly profitable, cash-generative subscription model. In 2025, operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5%, driven by revenue growth outpacing increases in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2069). The company’s cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% in 2024 to 52% in 2025, indicating improving operating leverage (10-k.txt:2114). Furthermore, the discontinuation of the DVD-by-mail service in 2023 had an immaterial impact on operations, allowing the company to focus entirely on its high-margin streaming core (10-k.txt:2064).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5**
While Netflix no longer reports average paying memberships, the earnings release provides direct evidence of strong customer retention. In Q3 2026, management noted that "membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast" (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). Additionally, management stated that member response to 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments, indicating that engagement—encompassing quantity, quality, and variety of viewing—remains healthy and that the company continues to deliver strong value (exhibit-99-1.txt:28, exhibit-99-1.txt:157). The score is not a 5 because the specific quantitative churn rate or retention percentage is not stated in the supplied filings.

**Organic Growth: 5/5**
Netflix exhibits strong organic growth across all geographic regions. In 2025, streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2059, 10-k.txt:2056). Regionally, UCAN grew 15%, EMEA grew 17%, LATAM grew 11%, and APAC grew 21% (10-k.txt:2087, 10-k.txt:2088, 10-k.txt:2089, 10-k.txt:2090). In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year (11% on an F/X neutral basis) to $12.9 billion, driven primarily by subscription revenue reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, as well as growth in advertising revenue (exhibit-99-1.txt:12, exhibit-99-1.txt:61).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5**
Netflix is actively expanding its service offerings and geographic reach. The company is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche of nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Additionally, Netflix is expanding its entertainment offering through new licensing partnerships, such as the TF1 partnership in France, which provides local series, film, news, and sports programming, and a new licensing deal with Disney that brings current and library series and films to the service (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Competitive Advantage: 5/5**
Netflix’s competitive advantage is supported by its differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced content and its global distribution network. The company serves an audience approaching one billion people, making it a strong partner for studios, networks, and creative talent (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:126). Non-English viewing has grown from under 10% of total viewing a decade ago to more than a third today, reflecting a decade-long commitment to creating content that resonates locally and travels globally (exhibit-99-1.txt:84). The company’s proprietary technology, including its Open Connect network and new TV UI, enables efficient content delivery and seamless integration of third-party content (10-k.txt:2109, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4/5**
Management has identified several catalysts for future growth, including the expansion of the advertising tier to new countries, the rollout of new ad product capabilities, and the introduction of new content slates. The company expects 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion, though this is slightly below the previous ~$3 billion estimate due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Moat Risk: 3/5**
Netflix faces risks from intense competition and regulatory changes. The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change, with Netflix competing against a broad set of activities for consumers' leisure time (10-k.txt:1725). Regulatory actions are also increasing, with some countries updating cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix, imposing investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas, which may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive (10-k.txt:1732). Additionally, the company faces risks related to intellectual property rights and the licensing of third-party content, which can vary in terms and conditions (10-k.txt:1730).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

**Future Developments**
Netflix expects full-year 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, representing 13% year-over-year growth, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company anticipates annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). In Q4 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $13.4 billion and an operating margin of 26.0%, which includes a ~120 basis point negative impact associated with recently announced headcount reductions (exhibit-99-1.txt:64). The company will continue to expand its entertainment offering through licensing and new ways to bring more third-party content to its service, such as the TF1 partnership in France (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). Netflix will also introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Strategic Recommendations**
Netflix should continue to focus on delivering differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment that sparks conversation and brings in more members (exhibit-99-1.txt:67). The company should leverage technology to improve all aspects of its service, including its product capabilities and ad tech stack (exhibit-99-1.txt:68, exhibit-99-1.txt:153). Additionally, Netflix should improve its monetization by expanding its advertising tier and increasing advertiser demand (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company should also continue to invest in its global content production capabilities to maintain its competitive advantage in non-English viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:84).

**Criterion Scores and Filing Evidence**
*   **Business-Model Durability: 5/5** - Operating margin expanded to 29.5% in 2025, and cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% to 52% (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2114).
*   **Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5** - Churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast in Q3 2026, and member response to 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:28).
*   **Organic Growth: 5/5** - 2025 streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2056, 10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5** - Netflix is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 and securing new licensing deals, such as with Disney and TF1 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).
*   **Competitive Advantage: 5/5** - Netflix serves an audience approaching one billion people and has grown non-English viewing to more than a third of total viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:84).
*   **Catalyst Evidence: 4/5** - The company expects 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion and is expanding its ad tech stack with new partnerships (exhibit-99-1.txt:65, exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat Risk: 3/5** - Netflix faces intense competition and increasing regulatory actions, including cultural support legislation and content catalog quotas (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1732).

**What Would Change My View**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a continued improvement in churn rates and a higher-than-expected rollout of ad product capabilities, leading to 2026 ad revenue exceeding the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). A weakening of my conclusion would be indicated by a decline in churn rates or a further delay in the rollout of ad product capabilities, resulting in 2026 ad revenue falling below the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of churn improving year-over-year and being better than forecast in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:61) has the strategic consequence of validating the company's pricing power and engagement model, which supports the sustainability of its 29.5% operating margin (10-k.txt:2061) and its ability to fund the next wave of entertainment investments (exhibit-99-1.txt:68).

# Overview

The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs (10-k.txt:1719). Management has shifted its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin, discontinuing the reporting of average paying memberships and average monthly revenue per paying membership (10-k.txt:2063). Netflix demonstrates strong business-model durability through its transition to a highly profitable, cash-generative subscription model. In 2025, operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5%, driven by revenue growth outpacing increases in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2069). The company’s cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% in 2024 to 52% in 2025, indicating improving operating leverage (10-k.txt:2114). Furthermore, the discontinuation of the DVD-by-mail service in 2023 had an immaterial impact on operations, allowing the company to focus entirely on its high-margin streaming core (10-k.txt:2064).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5**
While Netflix no longer reports average paying memberships, the earnings release provides direct evidence of strong customer retention. In Q3 2026, management noted that "membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast" (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). Additionally, management stated that member response to 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments, indicating that engagement—encompassing quantity, quality, and variety of viewing—remains healthy and that the company continues to deliver strong value (exhibit-99-1.txt:28, exhibit-99-1.txt:157). **Organic Growth: 5/5**
Netflix exhibits strong organic growth across all geographic regions. In 2025, streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2059, 10-k.txt:2056). Regionally, UCAN grew 15%, EMEA grew 17%, LATAM grew 11%, and APAC grew 21% (10-k.txt:2087, 10-k.txt:2088, 10-k.txt:2089, 10-k.txt:2090). **Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5**
Netflix is actively expanding its service offerings and geographic reach. The company is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche of nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Netflix’s competitive advantage is supported by its differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced content and its global distribution network. Non-English viewing has grown from under 10% of total viewing a decade ago to more than a third today, reflecting a decade-long commitment to creating content that resonates locally and travels globally (exhibit-99-1.txt:84). The company’s proprietary technology, including its Open Connect network and new TV UI, enables efficient content delivery and seamless integration of third-party content (10-k.txt:2109, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

*   **Organic Growth: 5/5** - 2025 streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2056, 10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5** - Netflix is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027 and securing new licensing deals, such as with Disney and TF1 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).
*   **Competitive Advantage: 5/5** - Netflix serves an audience approaching one billion people and has grown non-English viewing to more than a third of total viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:84).
*   **Catalyst Evidence: 4/5** - The company expects 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion and is expanding its ad tech stack with new partnerships (exhibit-99-1.txt:65, exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat Risk: 3/5** - Netflix faces intense competition and increasing regulatory actions, including cultural support legislation and content catalog quotas (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1732).

**What Would Change My View**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a continued improvement in churn rates and a higher-than-expected rollout of ad product capabilities, leading to 2026 ad revenue exceeding the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). A weakening of my conclusion would be indicated by a decline in churn rates or a further delay in the rollout of ad product capabilities, resulting in 2026 ad revenue falling below the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of churn improving year-over-year and being better than forecast in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:61) has the strategic consequence of validating the company's pricing power and engagement model, which supports the sustainability of its 29.5% operating margin (10-k.txt:2061) and its ability to fund the next wave of entertainment investments (exhibit-99-1.txt:68).

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving its primary revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a secondary, non-material revenue stream from advertisements, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721, 10-k.txt:2073). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs (10-k.txt:1719). In fiscal year 2025, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% year-over-year increase, and operating income of $13,326,603 thousand, resulting in an operating margin of 29.5% (10-k.txt:2058, 10-k.txt:2060, 10-k.txt:2061). Management has shifted its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin, discontinuing the reporting of average paying memberships and average monthly revenue per paying membership (10-k.txt:2063). The company maintains a competitive position by competing for consumers' "moments of truth" against a broad set of leisure activities, including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1726).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 5/5**
Netflix demonstrates strong business-model durability through its transition to a highly profitable, cash-generative subscription model. In 2025, operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5%, driven by revenue growth outpacing increases in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2069). The company’s cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% in 2024 to 52% in 2025, indicating improving operating leverage (10-k.txt:2114). Furthermore, the discontinuation of the DVD-by-mail service in 2023 had an immaterial impact on operations, allowing the company to focus entirely on its high-margin streaming core (10-k.txt:2064).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5**
While Netflix no longer reports average paying memberships, the earnings release provides direct evidence of strong customer retention. In Q3 2026, management noted that "membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast" (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). Additionally, management stated that member response to 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments, indicating that engagement—encompassing quantity, quality, and variety of viewing—remains healthy and that the company continues to deliver strong value (exhibit-99-1.txt:28, exhibit-99-1.txt:157). The score is not a 5 because the specific quantitative churn rate or retention percentage is not stated in the supplied filings.

**Organic Growth: 5/5**
Netflix exhibits strong organic growth across all geographic regions. In 2025, streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2059, 10-k.txt:2056). Regionally, UCAN grew 15%, EMEA grew 17%, LATAM grew 11%, and APAC grew 21% (10-k.txt:2087, 10-k.txt:2088, 10-k.txt:2089, 10-k.txt:2090). In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year (11% on an F/X neutral basis) to $12.9 billion, driven primarily by subscription revenue reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, as well as growth in advertising revenue (exhibit-99-1.txt:12, exhibit-99-1.txt:61).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5**
Netflix is actively expanding its service offerings and geographic reach. The company is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche of nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Additionally, Netflix is expanding its entertainment offering through new licensing partnerships, such as the TF1 partnership in France, which provides local series, film, news, and sports programming, and a new licensing deal with Disney that brings current and library series and films to the service (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Competitive Advantage: 5/5**
Netflix’s competitive advantage is supported by its differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced content and its global distribution network. The company serves an audience approaching one billion people, making it a strong partner for studios, networks, and creative talent (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:126). Non-English viewing has grown from under 10% of total viewing a decade ago to more than a third today, reflecting a decade-long commitment to creating content that resonates locally and travels globally (exhibit-99-1.txt:84). The company’s proprietary technology, including its Open Connect network and new TV UI, enables efficient content delivery and seamless integration of third-party content (10-k.txt:2109, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4/5**
Management has identified several catalysts for future growth, including the expansion of the advertising tier to new countries, the rollout of new ad product capabilities, and the introduction of new content slates. The company expects 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion, though this is slightly below the previous ~$3 billion estimate due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Moat Risk: 3/5**
Netflix faces risks from intense competition and regulatory changes. The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change, with Netflix competing against a broad set of activities for consumers' leisure time (10-k.txt:1725). Regulatory actions are also increasing, with some countries updating cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix, imposing investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas, which may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive (10-k.txt:1732). Additionally, the company faces risks related to intellectual property rights and the licensing of third-party content, which can vary in terms and conditions (10-k.txt:1730).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

**Future Developments**
Netflix expects full-year 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, representing 13% year-over-year growth, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company anticipates annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). In Q4 2026, Netflix expects revenue of $13.4 billion and an operating margin of 26.0%, which includes a ~120 basis point negative impact associated with recently announced headcount reductions (exhibit-99-1.txt:64). The company will continue to expand its entertainment offering through licensing and new ways to bring more third-party content to its service, such as the TF1 partnership in France (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). Netflix will also introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Strategic Recommendations**
Netflix should continue to focus on delivering differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment that sparks conversation and brings in more members (exhibit-99-1.txt:67). The company should leverage technology to improve all aspects of its service, including its product capabilities and ad tech stack (exhibit-99-1.txt:68, exhibit-99-1.txt:153). Additionally, Netflix should improve its monetization by expanding its advertising tier and increasing advertiser demand (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company should also continue to invest in its global content production capabilities to maintain its competitive advantage in non-English viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:84).

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving its primary revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a secondary, non-material revenue stream from advertisements, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721, 10-k.txt:2073). **Business-Model Durability: 5/5**
Netflix demonstrates strong business-model durability through its transition to a highly profitable, cash-generative subscription model. While Netflix no longer reports average paying memberships, the earnings release provides direct evidence of strong customer retention. In Q3 2026, management noted that "membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast" (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). Netflix exhibits strong organic growth across all geographic regions. Regionally, UCAN grew 15%, EMEA grew 17%, LATAM grew 11%, and APAC grew 21% (10-k.txt:2087, 10-k.txt:2088, 10-k.txt:2089, 10-k.txt:2090). In Q3 2026, revenue grew 12% year-over-year (11% on an F/X neutral basis) to $12.9 billion, driven primarily by subscription revenue reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, as well as growth in advertising revenue (exhibit-99-1.txt:12, exhibit-99-1.txt:61).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5**
Netflix is actively expanding its service offerings and geographic reach. The company is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027, with the first tranche of nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand launching in March 2027 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Netflix’s competitive advantage is supported by its differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced content and its global distribution network. The company serves an audience approaching one billion people, making it a strong partner for studios, networks, and creative talent (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:126). The company’s proprietary technology, including its Open Connect network and new TV UI, enables efficient content delivery and seamless integration of third-party content (10-k.txt:2109, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4/5**
Management has identified several catalysts for future growth, including the expansion of the advertising tier to new countries, the rollout of new ad product capabilities, and the introduction of new content slates. **Moat Risk: 3/5**
Netflix faces risks from intense competition and regulatory changes. The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change, with Netflix competing against a broad set of activities for consumers' leisure time (10-k.txt:1725). Regulatory actions are also increasing, with some countries updating cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix, imposing investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas, which may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive (10-k.txt:1732). 10-k.txt:1717: ABOUT US
10-k.txt:1718: Netflix, Inc. 10-k.txt:1724: COMPETITION
10-k.txt:1725: The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change. We also compete against entertainment video providers and content producers in obtaining content for our service, both for licensed content and for original content projects.
10-k.txt:1726: While consumers may maintain simultaneous relationships with multiple entertainment sources, we strive for consumers to choose us in their moments of free time. 10-k.txt:1729: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
10-k.txt:1730: We regard our trademarks, service marks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade dress, trade secrets, proprietary technologies and similar intellectual property as important to our success. 10-k.txt:1732: The media landscape and the internet delivery of content have seen growing regulatory action. Historically, media has been highly regulated in many countries. We aim to attract and retain great people — representing a broad array of perspectives and skills — to work together as a dream team. For more people and cultures to see themselves reflected on screen, it is important that our employee base represents the communities we serve.
10-k.txt:1736: We aim generally to pay our employees at their personal top of market, and they generally are able to choose the form of their compensation between cash and stock options. This permits employee compensation to be highly personalized and reflective of each employee's individual needs and preferences. exhibit-99-1.txt:60: Q3 Results and Forecast
exhibit-99-1.txt:61: Revenue in Q3 grew 12% year over year (+11% on a foreign exchange (F/X) neutral basis), and was in-line with our forecast. In Q3, revenue growth was driven primarily by subscription revenue, reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, growth in advertising revenue and a favorable impact from F/X rates, net of hedging. Membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast.
exhibit-99-1.txt:62: Q3’26 operating income totaled $4.5B (+37% year over year) and operating margin of 34.6% was up versus 28.2% in Q3’25. Both Q3 operating income and margin were ahead of forecast due primarily to the timing of expenses and the slight upside in revenue. As a result, diluted EPS for the quarter amounted to $0.87 vs. $0.59 in Q3’25 (+49% year over year).
exhibit-99-1.txt:63: As a reminder, the guidance we provide is our actual internal forecast at the time we report and we strive for accuracy. Our primary financial metrics are revenue for growth and operating margin for profitability. Our goal is to sustain healthy revenue growth, expand operating profit and margin, and deliver growing free cash flow.
exhibit-99-1.txt:64: In Q4, we expect revenue of $13.4 billion, which represents year over year growth of 12% (or 11% F/X neutral) driven by growth in memberships, pricing, and ad revenue. We project a Q4 operating margin of 26.0% which includes ~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions, and compares with 24.5% in the year ago quarter. These organizational changes enable us to continue to aggressively invest in high impact areas to improve our service, and drive growth and innovation.
exhibit-99-1.txt:65: Our guidance for Q4 means that for the full year 2026 we expect revenue of $51.1B, or growth of 13% (+12% on a F/X neutral basis). This is 0.2% below the mid-point of our prior 2026 revenue forecast range - while subscription revenue growth has outperformed our expectations, we currently expect 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7B vs. approximately $3B previously (due to slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities). We anticipate an operating margin of 31.5% for 2026 (31.4% based on F/X rates as of January 1, 2026) vs. 29.5% in 2025. Our updated 2026 margin guidance includes ~30 basis points negative impact associated with our Q4 headcount reductions. Our forecast implies annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:66: Our Focus
exhibit-99-1.txt:67: Our mission is to entertain the world while building a wildly successful business. Our strategy is simple: invest in differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment like Netflix originals that spark conversation, bring in more members, and make us a “must-have” service. We pair these originals, which anchor our service, with a broad, complementary selection of third-party programming, a great discovery experience, and leading global distribution. Together, this fuels engagement (quality, quantity, and variety of viewing) and, in turn, revenue and profit. The core of our service is streaming TV, film and live events, monetized via subscription and advertising. It represents the vast majority of our spending and nearly all of our revenue, and is the engine of our business for which we see a long runway of growth.
exhibit-99-1.txt:68: To successfully execute this strategy, we focus on three priorities: 1) delivering more entertainment value to our members, 2) leveraging technology to improve all aspects of our service, and 3) improving our monetization. # Course operating rules

These are harness rules. They are not part of a role's identity, values, or scoring criteria.

- Use only the evidence included in the JSON hand-off.
- Put an exact filing-line citation immediately after every filing number.
- Put an exact `calculations.json` citation immediately after every code-calculated number.
- Do not use a web number in the graded report.
- Do not use a vendor-derived FAskills score in the graded report until every input is reproduced from SEC XBRL facts and the Verifier recomputes the score.
- Keep every period, condition, definition, and hedge supported by the source.
- Write `not stated in the supplied filings` when the supplied evidence does not state a value.
- Never calculate inside a model role.
- Preserve GAAP and adjusted labels.
- Name the denominator definition for every margin and peer comparison.
- End each analyst output with one final nonblank line that begins exactly `Insight:`.
- The Insight must use exact supplied citation tokens and must not merely restate the earnings release's first paragraph.
- Do not write a four-digit year in an Insight unless the year has its own exact source citation.

# Overview

Netflix operates as a single-segment global entertainment service, deriving its primary revenue from monthly membership fees for streaming content, with a secondary, non-material revenue stream from advertisements, consumer products, and live experiences (10-k.txt:1721, 10-k.txt:2073). The company’s core strategy is to grow globally within the parameters of its operating margin target, utilizing a range of pricing plans—including an ad-supported tier—to meet diverse consumer needs (10-k.txt:1719). In the latest fiscal year, Netflix reported total revenues of $45,183,036 thousand, representing a 16% year-over-year increase, and operating income of $13,326,603 thousand, resulting in an operating margin of 29.5% (10-k.txt:2058, 10-k.txt:2060, 10-k.txt:2061). Management has shifted its primary financial metrics to revenue and operating margin, discontinuing the reporting of average paying memberships and average monthly revenue per paying membership (10-k.txt:2063). The company maintains a competitive position by competing for consumers' "moments of truth" against a broad set of leisure activities, including linear television, other streaming providers, video gaming, and social media (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1726).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 5/5**
Netflix demonstrates strong business-model durability through its transition to a highly profitable, cash-generative subscription model. In the latest fiscal year, operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points to 29.5%, driven by revenue growth outpacing increases in cost of revenues, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2069). The company’s cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% in the prior year to 52% in the latest fiscal year, indicating improving operating leverage (10-k.txt:2114). Furthermore, the discontinuation of the DVD-by-mail service in the prior fiscal year had an immaterial impact on operations, allowing the company to focus entirely on its high-margin streaming core (10-k.txt:2064).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5**
While Netflix no longer reports average paying memberships, the earnings release provides direct evidence of strong customer retention. In the current quarter, management noted that "membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast" (exhibit-99-1.txt:61). Additionally, management stated that member response to current year price changes is consistent with prior adjustments, indicating that engagement—encompassing quantity, quality, and variety of viewing—remains healthy and that the company continues to deliver strong value (exhibit-99-1.txt:28, exhibit-99-1.txt:157). The score is not a 5 because the specific quantitative churn rate or retention percentage is not stated in the supplied filings.

**Organic Growth: 5/5**
Netflix exhibits strong organic growth across all geographic regions. In the latest fiscal year, streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2059, 10-k.txt:2056). Regionally, UCAN grew 15%, EMEA grew 17%, LATAM grew 11%, and APAC grew 21% (10-k.txt:2087, 10-k.txt:2088, 10-k.txt:2089, 10-k.txt:2090). In the current quarter, revenue grew 12% year-over-year (11% on an F/X neutral basis) to $12.9 billion, driven primarily by subscription revenue reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, as well as growth in advertising revenue (exhibit-99-1.txt:12, exhibit-99-1.txt:61).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5**
Netflix is actively expanding its service offerings and geographic reach. The company is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in the next fiscal year, with the first tranche of nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru, and New Zealand launching in March of the next fiscal year (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Additionally, Netflix is expanding its entertainment offering through new licensing partnerships, such as the TF1 partnership in France, which provides local series, film, news, and sports programming, and a new licensing deal with Disney that brings current and library series and films to the service (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Competitive Advantage: 5/5**
Netflix’s competitive advantage is supported by its differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced content and its global distribution network. The company serves an audience approaching one billion people, making it a strong partner for studios, networks, and creative talent (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:126). Non-English viewing has grown from under 10% of total viewing a decade ago to more than a third today, reflecting a decade-long commitment to creating content that resonates locally and travels globally (exhibit-99-1.txt:84). The company’s proprietary technology, including its Open Connect network and new TV UI, enables efficient content delivery and seamless integration of third-party content (10-k.txt:2109, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4/5**
Management has identified several catalysts for future growth, including the expansion of the advertising tier to new countries, the rollout of new ad product capabilities, and the introduction of new content slates. The company expects next fiscal year ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion, though this is slightly below the previous ~$3 billion estimate due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company is also investing in its ad tech stack, extending programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals and securing new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA (exhibit-99-1.txt:153).

**Moat Risk: 3/5**
Netflix faces risks from intense competition and regulatory changes. The market for entertainment video is intensely competitive and subject to rapid change, with Netflix competing against a broad set of activities for consumers' leisure time (10-k.txt:1725). Regulatory actions are also increasing, with some countries updating cultural support legislation to include services like Netflix, imposing investment obligations, levies, and content catalog quotas, which may make operating in certain jurisdictions more expensive or restrictive (10-k.txt:1732). Additionally, the company faces risks related to intellectual property rights and the licensing of third-party content, which can vary in terms and conditions (10-k.txt:1730).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

**Future Developments**
Netflix expects full-year next fiscal year revenue of $51.1 billion, representing 13% year-over-year growth, and an operating margin of 31.5% (exhibit-99-1.txt:16, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). The company anticipates annual operating income growth of 20%+ for the next fiscal year (exhibit-99-1.txt:65). In the next quarter, Netflix expects revenue of $13.4 billion and an operating margin of 26.0%, which includes a ~120 basis point negative impact associated with recently announced headcount reductions (exhibit-99-1.txt:64). The company will continue to expand its entertainment offering through licensing and new ways to bring more third-party content to its service, such as the TF1 partnership in France (exhibit-99-1.txt:26). Netflix will also introduce its advertising tier to 15 new countries in the next fiscal year, with the first tranche launching in March of the next fiscal year (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Strategic Recommendations**
Netflix should continue to focus on delivering differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment that sparks conversation and brings in more members (exhibit-99-1.txt:67). The company should leverage technology to improve all aspects of its service, including its product capabilities and ad tech stack (exhibit-99-1.txt:68, exhibit-99-1.txt:153). Additionally, Netflix should improve its monetization by expanding its advertising tier and increasing advertiser demand (exhibit-99-1.txt:68). The company should also continue to invest in its global content production capabilities to maintain its competitive advantage in non-English viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:84).

**Criterion Scores and Filing Evidence**
*   **Business-Model Durability: 5/5** - Operating margin expanded to 29.5% in the latest fiscal year, and cost of revenues decreased as a percentage of revenues from 54% to 52% (10-k.txt:2061, 10-k.txt:2114).
*   **Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 4/5** - Churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast in the current quarter, and member response to current year price changes is consistent with prior adjustments (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:28).
*   **Organic Growth: 5/5** - Latest fiscal year streaming revenues increased 16% year-over-year, with constant currency revenue growth of 17% (10-k.txt:2056, 10-k.txt:2059).
*   **Expansion-Driven Growth: 4/5** - Netflix is expanding its advertising tier to 15 new countries in the next fiscal year and securing new licensing deals, such as with Disney and TF1 (exhibit-99-1.txt:153, exhibit-99-1.txt:129, exhibit-99-1.txt:152).
*   **Competitive Advantage: 5/5** - Netflix serves an audience approaching one billion people and has grown non-English viewing to more than a third of total viewing (exhibit-99-1.txt:26, exhibit-99-1.txt:84).
*   **Catalyst Evidence: 4/5** - The company expects next fiscal year ad revenue of ~$2.7 billion and is expanding its ad tech stack with new partnerships (exhibit-99-1.txt:65, exhibit-99-1.txt:153).
*   **Moat Risk: 3/5** - Netflix faces intense competition and increasing regulatory actions, including cultural support legislation and content catalog quotas (10-k.txt:1725, 10-k.txt:1732).

**What Would Change My View**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a continued improvement in churn rates and a higher-than-expected rollout of ad product capabilities, leading to next fiscal year ad revenue exceeding the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65). A weakening of my conclusion would be indicated by a decline in churn rates or a further delay in the rollout of ad product capabilities, resulting in next fiscal year ad revenue falling below the ~$2.7 billion estimate (exhibit-99-1.txt:61, exhibit-99-1.txt:65).

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of churn improving year-over-year and being better than forecast in the current quarter (exhibit-99-1.txt:61) has the strategic consequence of validating the company's pricing power and engagement model, which supports the sustainability of its 29.5% operating margin (10-k.txt:2061) and its ability to fund the next wave of entertainment investments (exhibit-99-1.txt:68).
